title: Researcher Sanjana Hattotuwa tells Sri Lanka's PM that flaws in LECO, Health Ministry and Police systems remain unresolved (claim)
date_note: The newswire.lk article is dated 24 November and gives no earlier day for the open letter; the researcher says he first alerted the authorities on October 24.
org: Government of Sri Lanka (LECO, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka Police)
summary: In an open letter to Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya, reported by newswire.lk, researcher Sanjana Hattotuwa says weaknesses he reported in October are still open in systems of the Lanka Electricity Company, the Ministry of Health and Sri Lanka Police, and that he rechecked in November and found them still open. The article reports no government response to these three systems.
plain: A researcher says in an open letter to Sri Lanka's prime minister that security weaknesses he reported in October are still open in electricity, health and police systems. The article reports no government reply on these.
exec: A researcher's open letter says weaknesses in Sri Lankan electricity, health and police systems remain open; the article reports no government reply on them.
impact: Per the researcher, customer, health-worker and police-complaint data could be exposed.

validation.note: One publisher (newswire.lk) relaying the researcher's own letter; no government statement read.

review.note: Compared title, claim status, Oct/Nov timeline, three systems, no-response statement against newswire.lk
